takeaway: The fundus is supplied by the short gastric arteries from the splenic artery. Lesser curvature: left and right gastric. Lower greater curvature: left and right gastroepiploic.

lines.text: Which arteries supply the fundus of the stomach?
The splenic artery runs in the gastrosplenic ligament.
It gives rise to the short gastric arteries, which supply the fundus and the upper greater curvature.
So the answer is the short gastric arteries.
The lesser curvature gets branches of the left and right gastric arteries.
The lower greater curvature gets the left and right gastroepiploic arteries:
the right from the gastroduodenal artery, and the left from the splenic artery.
